kill_fact: The catalyst is live, dated and unfired: the 10 November 8-K restates a 22 November 2026 PDUFA date, and EDGAR shows no Capricor 8-K after 10 November as of 16 November, so no early action and no new date. The priority review voucher is real, because the rare-pediatric-disease voucher program was reauthorized to 30 September 2029 in the FY2026 appropriations act. Two load-bearing corrections. (1) The record says the July inspection 'drew no follow-up'. It left out that the FDA issued a Form 483 with one observation on HOPE-3 trial conduct, covering standard operating procedures, documentation practices, vendor oversight and the timeliness of audit reports. Capricor has responded and is 'awaiting the Agency's feedback' (10-Q). That is an open finding about how the pivotal trial was run, on a trial whose analysis plan the FDA's reviewers already dispute, and it is a ready reason for a refusal letter that the bull side never prices. (2) The $3.00 cash floor is overstated. Unrestricted cash plus marketable securities was $197.6M at 30 September ($44.3M cash and $153.3M securities; the remaining ~$1M of the $198.5M is restricted). The nine-month cash burn was $117.6M, made up of $96.4M operating and ~$21.2M capex, or about $13.1M a month. That leaves about $176M by 20 November. Subtracting $16.4M of payables and accrued expenses and some wind-down cost, against $26.1M of non-cancellable purchase orders and severance, gives about $155M on 58.14M shares (not 57.9M), or about $2.70 a share. The approval value of about $30 stays within a defensible range, so the asymmetry survives. EV = 0.26 x $30 + 0.74 x $2.70 = about $9.80, roughly 17% above $8.39, with breakeven approval odds near 21% against 26%. The edge is thin and sits inside the error of judging a contested trial.
